fields.subnational_unit: Piura region, northern coastal Peru (about 2 million inhabitants); Sullana and Sechura districts cited
fields.population: households in Piura (urban, peri-urban and dispersed rural) as described in the literature and institutional data; stakeholders ANA, MVCS, OTASS, regional and local governments
fields.sample_size: targeted literature review, March-August 2025: 40 peer-reviewed articles (2017-2025, Q1/Q2 journals) identified, 21 retained; plus OECD, UN-Water, ANA, MVCS, OTASS and national and regional planning documents
fields.effect_measure: structured documentary analysis (Codina method) with a comparative reading matrix; three thematic blocks: territorial disparities, structural and institutional drivers, governance interventions; no quantitative synthesis
fields.effect_estimate: Piped coverage above 70% in Piura but supply highly intermittent (often under 8 hours a day; rural dispersed areas under 3 hours), arsenic, pesticide and E. coli contamination even in tap-water households, storage-related vulnerability. Drivers: overlapping mandates, limited local technical capacity, weak or absent monitoring systems, fragmented governance; isolated university and private pilot projects lack institutional integration and scaling mechanisms; the literature on governance interventions in rural Peru is thin. Calls for territorialised planning, coordination and inclusive governance within OECD Principles and IWRM. No effect estimate.
fields.model_type: structured documentary analysis of academic literature and institutional data
fields.study_design: targeted (non-systematic) literature and documentary review with a territorial case focus (MDPI article type Review)
fields.section: Full text (MDPI Sustainability 17(16):7542): Abstract; Methods 2.1-2.3; Results 3.1-3.3; Discussion 4; Conclusions 5
fields.exact_location: Abstract p1; methods p6-7 (2.1-2.3); results 3.1-3.3 p8-12; limitations 4.4

evidence_level: Secondary evidence: a targeted documentary review (21 articles retained of 40, plus OECD, UN-Water, ANA and ministry documents) of drinking-water access inequality and governance in Piura, Peru, read in full text 2026-10-04. Coverage above 70% but intermittent supply; fragmented mandates and weak monitoring. Not a primary study and not a registered systematic review; the CASP qualitative tool applied earlier does not fit.
